params.name: e
randint: 5 if b == 2 else (3 if b == 3 else 2)

solution: The exponents are $t-1$, $t$ and $t+1$. Rewrite the last two terms so that each contains the smallest power ${=b}^{t-1}$, using $a^{m+n}=a^{m}\cdot a^{n}$: ${=b}^{t}={=b}^{t-1}\cdot {=b}$ and ${=b}^{t+1}={=b}^{t-1}\cdot {=b}^{2}$.
Write the right-hand side as a power of ${=b}$: ${=b}^{t-1}={=b}^{{=e}}$.
The bases are the same, so equate the exponents: $t-1={=e}$.
notes: Advanced twist: three terms with exponents t-1, t and t+1, so the common factor is the smallest power b^(t-1) and the exponent equation that ends the solution is linear (t-1 = e) instead of t = e. It uses only the book's method from we10 (rewrite each term with a^(m+n) = a^m * a^n, take out the common factor, simplify, write the right side as a power of the same prime base, equate exponents), extended to three terms and a lowered exponent. A student who prefers to factor out b^t and work with the fraction 1/b gets the same unique answer. Parameter space: b = 2 with e in 1..5, b = 3 with e in 1..3, b = 5 with e in 1..2, ten instances. I checked all ten by brute force: the left side equals n for exactly one integer t, and it is e + 1 (so t runs from 2 to 6). Largest n is 775 (5^2 * 31). Numeric answer is a whole number. No mcq, for the same reason as the basic family: the catalogue holds no misconceptions for this objective.
